fields.what: An open multi-system FPGA platform on the Terasic DE10-Nano. Its Minimig-AGA core covers OCS/ECS/AGA plus CDTV and partial CD32, with a 68000 or 68020 soft-CPU, up to 2 MB chip plus 384 MB fast RAM, four floppies (ADF, SCP and IPF), four IDE devices including CD-ROM, RTG to 1920×1080, A2065 Ethernet, a shared Linux↔Amiga folder and MIDI.
fields.why: For many enthusiasts the reference low-latency, highly configurable Amiga recreation. A wave of compatible boards (MiSTer Pi, QMTECH clones and consolised systems such as the MiSTer Multisystem 2) brought the entry price well below a genuine DE10-Nano setup.

fields.what: A 68000-socket adapter carrying a Raspberry Pi (3A+ or Zero 2) for the A500, A500+, A1000 and A2000, with a PiStorm600 variant for the A600. fields.why: Open hardware and software (MIT, BSD and MPL 2.0) that collapsed the cost of a fast Amiga from hundreds to tens: the single most disruptive hardware project of the 2020s.
fields.by: Claude "captain-amygdala" Schwarz & community; Emu68 by Michal Schulz

fields.name: 2026 Amiga Corporation–Hyperion settlement
fields.by: Amiga Corporation & Hyperion Entertainment BV
fields.what: Signed on 5 June 2026 and announced on 4 August, the settlement ends all litigation and replaces the 2009 agreement. Hyperion keeps the AmigaOS 4 code it developed and gets an exclusive, royalty-free licence to continue AmigaOS 4 on PowerPC and any CPU architecture except 68K, including use of the AmigaOne name; its registrations and applications for Amiga marks, AmigaOS and AmigaOne among them, pass to Amiga Corporation. On 68K its rights are transitional: AmigaOS 3.2 and 3.3 only as upgrades for licensed systems, regular sales ending at the later of 31 December 2026 or 16 months after 3.3 ships, and all distribution ending by 31 December 2027. Hyperion hands Amiga the source, history and documentation of AmigaOS 3.1–3.1.4 (excluding OS4 code backported into 3.2/3.3), and its developers are free to work with Amiga. Hyperion says it will complete AmigaOS 3.3 and 4.2.
fields.why: The most consequential development in decades: it ends the legal paralysis, frees AmigaOS 4 from PowerPC, and returns 68K AmigaOS stewardship to Amiga Corporation. Announced alongside it, a separate agreement concluded within weeks has Amiga recognise Commodore's ownership of the Commodore marks and license it CBM 8-bit software; Amiga's named licensees include A1200.NET, Antstream Arcade, Blaze Entertainment, Cloanto, Retro Games, Simulant Systems and SpecNext.

description: Several details are wrong or unsupported. (1) Signing and announcement: amiga-news obtained the full agreement, which was signed on 5 June 2026, and both companies announced it on 4 August 2026. (2) The Commodore agreement was not 'same-day': Amiga Corporation says the two agreements were 'concluded within a few weeks of one another' and announced together. (3) I found no source for 'over twenty registrations'. What is reported is that Hyperion transfers its registrations for the covered Amiga marks, plus its AmigaOS and AmigaOne applications, to Amiga Corporation. (4) Hyperion's licence is exclusive, worldwide and royalty-free for AmigaOS 4 on PowerPC and 'any CPU architecture apart from 68K', with an exclusive licence to use the AmigaOne name, so 'exclusive rights to the AmigaOne brand' overstates it. (5) For 68k, AmigaOS 3.2/3.3 may be distributed only as upgrades for licensed systems. Regular sales end at the later of 31 Dec 2026 or 16 months after 3.3 ships, and distribution ends no later than 31 Dec 2027. (6) The sources handed over are AmigaOS 3.1–3.1.4 with fixes, history and documentation, excluding OS4 code backported into 3.2/3.3, not 'the sources' of 3.2/3.3. fields.name: Cloanto and Amiga Corporation reunite the Amiga IP
fields.what: Cloanto, long the publisher of Amiga Forever, completed its acquisition of the Commodore-era Amiga copyrights (works up to 1993, including AmigaOS 3.1 and earlier) from Amiga, Inc. in 2012. On 1 February 2019, C-A Acquisition Corp., led by Cloanto's Mike Battilana, bought Amiga, Inc.'s remaining IP including the trademarks, and was renamed Amiga Corporation in 2020. By 2026 Amiga Corporation held the copyrights and trademarks, with Cloanto as a licensee, and a settlement effective June 2026 ended its litigation with Hyperion: Hyperion keeps AmigaOS 4, and 68k AmigaOS returns to Amiga Corporation once Hyperion's AmigaOS 3.2/3.3 sales window closes.
fields.why: For the first time since 1994, the historic copyrights and the trademarks sit with one owner that actively licenses them, and the 2026 settlement finally separated the 68k and PowerPC AmigaOS lines after years of litigation.

fields.what: Relations broke down after Amiga Inc.'s US Amiga trademark lapsed in 2016. Cloanto sued Hyperion in the US in December 2017, later joined by the other Amiga parties, and Hyperion counter-sued in March 2018 while shipping AmigaOS 3.1.4 (2018) and 3.2 (2021) for classic machines. Settlement terms reported to the court in January 2021 never closed; Hyperion won the first round in 2023, but the Ninth Circuit revived the copyright claims in 2025. After a pause in March 2026, Hyperion and Amiga Corporation signed a new settlement on 5 June 2026, announced on 4 August, which replaced the 2009 agreement and ended all their disputes.
fields.why: It froze parts of the ecosystem for most of a decade. AmigaOS 3.2 sales were interrupted, developers were caught between the parties, and in 2025 Retro Games Ltd publicly blamed the dispute for holding up its full-size Amiga, later THEA1200.

fields.by: Haage & Partner (Sam Jordan, Hans-Joerg & Thomas Frieden); later Hyperion Entertainment and A-EON Technology

fields.by: 7-bit / Retro 7-bit (PL)

fields.by: Commodore (Ed Hepler, Tim McDonald) with Hewlett-Packard
fields.what: A two-chip PA-RISC design: Nathaniel, a CPU/rendering chip with an in-house 64-bit PA-RISC core, blitter, Copper and audio, plus Natalie, a video chip. fields.name: The Settlers II: Gold Edition (Amiga)
fields.by: Look Behind You (Steffen Häuser), licensed by Ubisoft
fields.what: An officially licensed Amiga version of Blue Byte's 1996 city-building strategy game, released on 18 October 2025 at Amiga40 in Mönchengladbach after a gamescom 2025 preview. It needs an AGA Amiga with a 68040 at 40 MHz and 32 MB fast RAM, with PowerPC builds for AmigaOS 4.1 and AmigaOS 3.2 with WarpUP. Digital, boxed and a sold-out 100-copy wooden Collector's Edition were offered; updates in May 2026 improved the 68k, PPC and OS4 versions.
fields.why: A game that famously skipped the Amiga in 1996 finally shipped for it, with the rights holder's licence. It is the clearest example of a modern commercial Amiga release backed by a major publisher, and a flagship of the Amiga40 event.

fields.name: Evercade Amiga cartridges
fields.by: Blaze Entertainment with Team17, The Bitmap Brothers and other publishers
fields.what: A line of licensed Evercade cartridges, packaged in blue home-computer cases, running Amiga games through emulation on Blaze's handheld and TV systems with save states and PAL 50 Hz. Team17 Collection 1 (May 2023) was the first, with ten Team17 titles; The Bitmap Brothers Collection 2 (September 2024, cartridge C08) added Cadaver, Cadaver: The Payoff, Gods, Magic Pockets, The Chaos Engine 2 and the PlayStation Z.
fields.why: The first legal Amiga emulation on a handheld format, announced at Amiga37 in October 2022 and part of the licensing network that now includes Retro Games Ltd and Blaze in the 2026 settlement. It sits next to the THEA mini-computers as another consumer route to licensed Amiga games.

fields.name: Kickstart Amiga Expo
fields.by: Kickstart Amiga Group (founded by Ravi Abbott of The Retro Hour)
fields.what: The UK's biggest Amiga show, a combined trade show, user-group meeting and talks programme. Kickstart 01 ran in July 2023 at Meadow Lane, Nottingham; Kickstart 02 on 29-30 June 2024 had about 800 attendees expected; a 40th-anniversary Kickstart followed in September 2025; and Kickstart Expo 3.0 moved to The Reach Conference Centre in Derby on 7-8 August 2026, where Amiga Corporation outlined its AmigaOS 3 plans. Attendees receive free Amiga Forever and C64 Forever licences.
fields.why: The principal British counterpart to the Mönchengladbach and Sacramento shows, and where exclusive news such as Amiga Corporation's RTG plans and Commodore updates broke. The catalogue covers AmiWest and Amiga37-40 but not this show.
